daily_brief: European leaders convened in Dublin for a European Political Community summit focused on continental security, while US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff traveled to Moscow to meet President Putin following inconclusive Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi [BBC, Globe and Mail, France 24]. The diplomatic push comes as Ukraine faces severe infrastructure strain, with President Zelensky reporting renewed disruptions to military Starlink services that he says are hindering drone interception capabilities [BBC, Financial Times]. Meanwhile, Nvidia faces a leadership crisis as CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair has sparked national security concerns, with US officials reportedly alleging his former partner Alice Huang was working for Chinese intelligence [Nikkei Asia, The Hindu, Globe and Mail]. In a historic political shift, Democrat Scott Colom won Mississippi's US Senate race by fewer than 5,000 votes, becoming the first Black senator from the state since Reconstruction and expanding the Democratic Senate majority to 55 seats [BBC]. At COP31 in Turkey, African nations saw their proposal to triple climate adaptation finance blocked from the formal agenda by wealthy nations, while Médecins Sans Frontières warned that hundreds of millions in Ebola response funding is not reaching frontline workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where over 5,400 have died [RFI, BBC].

top_stories.headline: US Envoys Meet Putin in Moscow as Ukraine Peace Talks Yield Limited Progress
bullets: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Thursday, following two days of US-mediated talks between Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi
The Abu Dhabi talks produced no major breakthrough aside from an agreement for a large prisoner exchange, with the exact number still to be announced

Kushner and Witkoff are scheduled to travel to Dublin to meet with Ukrainian President Zelensky, where over 40 European leaders are gathering for a European Political Community summit on continental security
The US is seeking European participation in negotiations, but Moscow has resisted including European countries in direct talks

top_stories.headline: Ukraine Reports Renewed Starlink Disruptions Amid Russian Attacks on Power Grid
bullets: President Zelensky said Ukraine's military faces 'systematic' restrictions to SpaceX's military-grade Starshield service, hampering efforts to intercept Russian jet-powered drones
The disruption has been ongoing for several days; a similar incident in late October lasted about a week before being resolved, with unclear explanations from US officials and SpaceX

Russian attacks on Ukraine's energy grid have intensified, with some Kyiv families experiencing power outages of up to 20 hours; officials warn life will become unsustainable if power cannot be maintained for at least four hours daily
Ukraine has responded by striking Russian oil refineries

top_stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Faces Board Review Amid Affair and Espionage Allegations
bullets: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair with Alice Huang (Huang Le), a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed
US officials reportedly believe Alice Huang was working for Chinese intelligence; Beijing has rejected the spying allegations
Nvidia's board of directors met to discuss Huang's situation, with speculation he may be ousted; multiple US media outlets reported he had a second relationship with an Nvidia vice president
Alice Huang visited Taiwan eight times in 2024-2025 using a Hong Kong passport; Megaspeed pledged to cooperate with US investigations

top_stories.headline: Democrat Scott Colom Wins Mississippi Senate Race, First Black Senator From State Since 1881
bullets: Scott Colom defeated Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by fewer than 5,000 votes out of nearly one million cast, winning 49.2% to 48.7%
Colom becomes the first Black person from Mississippi seated in the US Senate since Blanche Bruce served from 1875 to 1881
The victory gives Democrats 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with a race in Alaska still to be called
The contest was not considered competitive until the final weeks, as Trump won Mississippi by more than 22 points in 2024

top_stories.headline: MSF Warns Ebola Response Funds Not Reaching Frontlines as DRC Death Toll Exceeds 5,400
bullets: Médecins Sans Frontières reported that the DRC Ebola outbreak 'remains out of control' six months after detection, with more than 5,400 dead and 11,000 infected
The charity said frontline workers are going unpaid, lack proper training, face supply shortages, and some ambulances have run out of fuel

Africa CDC reported last month that $700 million of $962 million disbursed for Ebola response was unaccounted for, though it characterized this as a transparency failure rather than confirmed embezzlement
MSF urged the Congolese government and UN agencies to strengthen oversight and accountability
